items.title: US to designate Brazil's two largest gangs as terrorist organizations

featured_image.name: Death toll in Brazil police raid on drug gang in Rio rises

items.description:
The United States announced Thursday that it will classify Brazil's two largest criminal organizations — the Primeiro Comando da Capital (PCC) and the Comando Vermelho (Red Command) — as Foreign Terrorist Organizations, a move that carries sweeping financial and legal consequences and is expected to deepen friction between Washington and Brasília.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio said in a statement that the formal FTO designation will take effect on June 5. In the meantime, the State Department has already classified both gangs as "Specially Designated Global Terrorists," immediately subjecting them to U.S. sanctions.[1][2][3]

items.title: Anthropic raises $65B at $965B valuation, topping OpenAI

featured_image.name: Anthropic set to hit $10.9 billion in revenue in Q2, source ...

items.description:
Anthropic has closed a $65 billion Series H funding round at a post-money valuation of $965 billion, making it the most valuable AI startup in the world and surpassing rival OpenAI, Bloomberg reported on Thursday.[1]

The round was co-led by Altimeter Capital, Dragoneer, Greenoaks, and Sequoia Capital, with additional participation from Capital Group, Coatue, and D1 Capital Partners. The deal caps a whirlwind fundraising process that began in late April, when Anthropic first signaled to investors it was targeting a valuation above $900 billion.[2][3][4][1]

items.title: US and Iran reportedly reach 60-day MOU deal awaiting Trump's approval

featured_image.name: What's inside the Iran deal Trump is close to signing

items.description:
Negotiators from the United States and Iran have reached an agreement on a 60-day memorandum of understanding to extend their ceasefire and begin negotiations over Iran's nuclear program, but President Donald Trump still needs to give final approval, Axios reported on Thursday, citing two U.S. officials.[1]

The reported breakthrough came on a day of renewed violence. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said it struck a U.S. airbase early Thursday in retaliation for American strikes near the port city of Bandar Abbas, where U.S. forces had intercepted four Iranian attack drones and hit a ground-control station threatening commercial shipping near the Strait of Hormuz.[2][3][4]

items.title: Israel strikes Beirut suburb targeting Iranian militia missile commander

featured_image.name: Israel strikes Beirut southern suburb ahead of crucial Washington talks

items.description:
Israel's air force carried out a targeted strike on the Choueifat area on the outskirts of Beirut's southern suburbs on Thursday afternoon, the first such attack near the Lebanese capital in weeks, as the military said it was targeting the head of the missile unit in the Imam Hussein Division, an Iran-linked militia operating alongside Hezbollah.[1][2][3]

The target was identified as Ali al-Husseini, described by Israeli Army Radio as the commander of the rocket system within the Imam Hussein Division. It was not immediately clear whether al-Husseini was killed in the strike. The attack hit a building in Choueifat, with at least one person reported killed and several wounded, according to Lebanese media reports.[4][2][5][3]

items.title: Iran's IRGC says it struck US airbase near Bandar Abbas

featured_image.name: Iran's IRGC say they targeted US airbase after strike near Bandar Abbas -  World - Aaj English TV

items.description:
The United States and Iran exchanged fresh military strikes on Thursday near the Strait of Hormuz, the most serious escalation since a ceasefire took effect on April 8, rattling energy markets and casting doubt over negotiations to end the conflict.

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said it targeted a US airbase early Thursday from which American forces had launched strikes on southern Iran near Bandar Abbas airport, according to Reuters and the Tasnim news agency. The IRGC described the attack as "a serious warning" to the United States. US Central Command had previously carried out what it termed "self-defense strikes" targeting missile launch sites and Iranian vessels attempting to lay mines near the strait.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: U.S. launches new airstrikes in southern Iran amid stalled ceasefire talks

featured_image.name: US forces strike Iranian boats, launch sites in Bandar Abbas

items.description:
The U.S. military carried out new airstrikes in southern Iran targeting a military site believed to pose a threat to American forces and commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, a U.S. official confirmed on Wednesday. U.S. forces also intercepted and shot down multiple Iranian drones in the region, according to ABC News.[1]

The strikes come as negotiations between Washington and Tehran over a potential peace deal remain unsettled. Speaking at a cabinet meeting Wednesday, President Donald Trump said Iran "wants very much to make a deal" but added, "We're not satisfied with it, but that we will be. Either that or we'll have to just finish the job".[1]

items.title: EU sets June 16 date to open Ukraine accession talks

featured_image.name: EU launches formal accession negotiations with Ukraine and Moldova

items.description: The European Commission is preparing to propose the formal opening of the first cluster of EU membership negotiations with Ukraine and Moldova on June 16, with EU leaders expected to endorse the move at their summit on June 18-19, according to the Kyiv Post. The development comes after nearly two years of deadlock caused by Hungary's veto under former Prime Minister Viktor Orbán.[1]

items.title: Oil supertankers cross Hormuz as strait traffic inches up

featured_image.name: Why shadow tankers are the only ships still moving through the Strait of  Hormuz

items.description:
Commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz showed faint signs of life this week as a COSCO oil products tanker navigated the waterway on Wednesday, a day after two non-Iranian crude supertankers made the crossing — the first time in a week that roughly four million barrels of unsanctioned crude were seen transiting the chokepoint.

The Singapore-linked Eagle Veracruz and Greek-owned Nissos Keros were both observed crossing Hormuz early on Tuesday, carrying crude from Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates respectively, according to vessel-tracking data reported by Bloomberg. Overall, five vessels traversed Hormuz in both directions on Tuesday, Bloomberg reported.[1][2]

items.title: White House calls leaked Iran draft deal a 'fabrication'

featured_image.name: Hormuz Flows May Return to Normal Within Month of Deal: Iran TV

items.description: Iranian state television reported on Wednesday that it had obtained a draft of an "initial, unofficial" framework for a memorandum of understanding between the United States and Iran that would restore commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz to pre-war levels within one month of finalization. The White House quickly pushed back, calling the Iranian report a "total fabrication".[1][2][3]
